newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Faulding to bid for U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: Faulding to bid for U.S. unit.

text.p: Australian pharmaceutical group F H Faulding & Co Ltd said it planned to make a US12 a share merger offer for its listed U.S. subsidiary, Faulding Inc.
Faulding said it will fund the merger by means of a rights issue. It gave no details of the issue.
Faulding said it now owns about 62 percent of the common stock of Faulding Inc and about 73 percent on a fully-diluted basis.
About 5.82 million shares of Faulding Inc's common stock are owned by the public, it said.

"The proposal, which was made in a letter delivered today to Faulding Inc, involves a cash merger in which a newly formed wholly owned subsidiary of Faulding would be merged into Faulding Inc and would acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares that are not currently owned by at a price of US$12 per share in cash," Faulding said.

Ed Tweddell, group managing director/chief executive officer of Faulding and chairman of Faulding Inc, indicated that he planned to seek a meeting of the board of Faulding Inc as soon as possible and would propose it appoint a committee of independent directors to consider Faulding's proposal, the
Faulding has appointed Dillon, Read & Co Inc to act as its investment banker in this transaction, it said.
"Faulding intends to fund the merger by means of a rights issue for which an underwriting offer has been received from J B Were & Son," it added.
Faulding Inc shares last traded at 10-3/4 on May 30.
